title: Features
lede: N.I.N.A. Polaris is a browser-controlled astrophotography platform that runs on a Raspberry Pi, mini-PC, or any small Linux or Windows host on your network. Point any device, laptop, tablet, or phone, at the host and you get the full equipment, capture, and processing workflow with no desktop application to install. Everything below runs from a single web UI, organized by sidebar panel.

glance.label: Runs anywhere small
glance.text: Raspberry Pi 4/5, Orange Pi, x86 mini-PCs and sticks, or a Windows box. ARM64, ARMHF, and x86-64 are all supported.

glance.label: Browser-native
glance.text: no app to install on the client; works on phones, tablets, and laptops over WiFi.

glance.label: Hardware-agnostic
glance.text: INDI, ASCOM Alpaca, ASCOM Platform (Windows COM), and native vendor SDKs (ZWO, Svbony, Player One, ToupTek, Canon/Nikon/Sony DSLR) all in one app.

glance.label: Acquire and process in one place
glance.text: from polar alignment through capture, live stacking, calibration, integration, AI cleanup, and a final non-destructive editor pass with JPEG/PNG/TIFF export.

glance.label: Offline-first
glance.text: bundled deep-sky catalog, star catalog, and sky map work with no internet at the telescope.

glance.label: Self-updating
glance.text: on Pi/SBC .deb installs, a one-click in-app update from GitHub releases.

sections.title: HOME
sections.intro: The landing dashboard shown on connect.

items.label: Session summary
items.text: active rig, connection status of each device, and current activity at a glance.

items.label: Quick navigation
items.text: jump straight into the panel you need.

items.label: Host info
items.text: model, OS, architecture, core count, and CPU of the machine running Polaris.

sections.title: RIGS
sections.intro: Multi-rig equipment hub. Define several telescope setups (rigs) and switch between them in one click.

items.label: Multi-rig profiles
items.text: save each optical train (main scope, camera, mount, guider, accessories) as a named rig; the whole app retargets when you switch the active rig.

items.label: Per-role device cards
items.text: Main Telescope, Camera, Mount, Focuser, Filter Wheel, Guidescope, Guide Camera, Guide Focuser, Rotator, Flat Panel, Dome, and Weather, each with connect/disconnect and live status.

items.label: Auxiliary camera and focuser
items.text: a second imaging camera on the same mount with its own optics, exposure, and gain, captured in parallel into a separate aux folder and focusable from the FOCUS tab (manual or Auto V-curve).

items.label: Gain and ISO aware
items.text: astronomy cameras show analogue gain with an ISO explainer; DSLR and mirrorless bodies (gphoto on Linux) get a real ISO dropdown.

items.label: Connection backends in one place
items.text: INDI (TCP/XML) full native client; ASCOM Alpaca (HTTP) auto-discovery and connect; ASCOM Platform (COM) Windows-only direct driver access; native vendor SDKs (ZWO ASI, Svbony, Player One, ToupTek, and Altair) driven directly; DSLR via Canon, Nikon, and Sony on Windows, gphoto2 on Linux.

items.label: Per-rig optical data
items.text: main and guider focal length (auto-updated from plate solves), a filter offsets table, and per-camera quirk overrides (Bayer pattern, vertical flip) for cameras that report wrong metadata.

items.label: Robust INDI handling
items.text: ack-based property writes, configurable per-device pre-connect delays, and idempotent connect logic.

items.label: Embedded INDI Drivers Manager
items.text: the indi-web UI inside the panel, so you can add or remove INDI drivers and start or stop the indiserver without SSH.

items.label: Live INDI property tree
items.text: browse and set any INDI property directly.

sections.title: POLAR
sections.intro: Get the mount's polar axis aligned before the night starts.

items.label: TPPA (Three-Point Polar Alignment)
items.text: plate-solve-driven. Capture, slew, and solve at three points, then a live error vector tells you which way to turn the altitude and azimuth bolts.

items.label: Refinement mode
items.text: a continuous capture and solve loop with an on-screen error overlay that updates as you adjust, so you converge to near-zero.

items.label: Rudimentary mode
items.text: single-target alignment helper for setups without a clear view of the celestial pole.

sections.title: SKY
sections.intro: Plan what to shoot and where to point.

items.label: Offline sky map
items.text: interactive sky atlas with bundled star data; works with no internet at the scope.

items.label: Offline DSS sky imagery
items.text: an optional real DSS photo background for the map that works fully offline at the telescope (provisionable, roughly 30 MB to 400 MB), with an online fallback when you have internet.

items.label: Target search
items.text: find deep-sky objects by name or catalog from the bundled DSO database, or enter manual RA/DEC.

items.label: DSO preview thumbnails
items.text: a small offline DSS thumbnail on every search result and atlas card, so galaxies and nebulae are easy to tell apart at a glance.

items.label: FOV overlays and framing
items.text: draw your camera's field of view on the map, rotate it, and drag to frame a target; the blue (mount) and red (target) rectangles track plate-solve results, plus a pink rectangle for the auxiliary camera's field when an Auxiliary Camera System is configured.

items.label: Aux FOV confirmation
items.text: a plate solve from SKY fires a parallel solve on the auxiliary camera's own hardware, so the pink rectangle reflects the true rotation and scale the aux photo will come out with.

items.label: Slew & center
items.text: send the mount to a target and plate-solve-center on it.

items.label: Mosaic planner
items.text: lay out multi-panel mosaics over a target, with a live preview of the tile grid drawn right on the sky map as you adjust columns, rows, and overlap.

items.label: Tonight
items.text: altitude curves and the best objects to image for your location and date, with twilight and night windows; the ranking also surfaces large emission and dark nebulae that carry size but no stellar magnitude.

items.label: Weather
items.text: current conditions and forecast for the observing site.

items.label: Stellarium sync
items.text: drive the view from and to a Stellarium instance.

sections.title: FOCUS
sections.intro: Achieve and verify focus, and diagnose the optical train.

items.label: Manual focus
items.text: step the focuser in and out with a live preview canvas and real-time HFR (half-flux radius) plus Laplacian-variance sharpness readout.

items.label: Auto-focus
items.text: automated V-curve sweep with parabola fit; robust on heavy defocus, with an HFR-vs-position chart of the run. An optical-train selector runs the sweep on the main, auxiliary, or guide camera and focuser pair.

items.label: Aux and guide focusing
items.text: Camera and Focuser source switches (Primary, Auxiliary, or Guide) target a second OTA or a motorised guide scope; the manual jog (position, range, GoTo, abort) follows the selected motor.

items.label: Bahtinov mask helper
items.text: overlay analysis of a Bahtinov diffraction pattern for precise manual focus.

items.label: Field analysis tools
items.text: shared capture with multiple views. Tilt: a sensor-tilt map from corner-vs-center star sizes. Aberration Inspector: a 3x3 mosaic of 1:1 corner and center crops to judge coma, astigmatism, and backfocus. Inspector: full-field star metrics (eccentricity, FWHM) to spot collimation and spacing problems.

items.label: Sensor analysis
items.text: characterize the camera sensor itself.

sections.title: GUIDE
sections.intro: Keep stars round during long exposures, with two interchangeable backends.

items.label: Native guider
items.text: PHD2's guiding math ported to C#, driving the rig's guide camera and mount directly with no external PHD2 process. Multi-star guiding, per-equipment calibration save and restore, dithering with ASIAIR-style settle readout, star-lost detection with a responsive watchdog, a predictive algorithm option (periodic-error and drift modeling), and meridian-flip awareness.

items.label: ZFilter algorithm
items.text: a low-pass guide algorithm ported from PHD2 that smooths guide noise and seeing while still chasing slow drift, with a per-rig exposure-factor tuning to dial in responsiveness for your gear.

items.label: PHD2 integration
items.text: full control of an external PHD2. Connect, manage profiles and equipment, set exposure, launch and shutdown, smart calibration orchestration, guiding-algorithm presets, and the embedded PHD2 GUI in the browser via xpra (Linux) or noVNC.

items.label: Live guiding telemetry
items.text: RA/Dec error graph, RMS, and dither/settle state surfaced in the top status bar.

sections.title: PREVIEW
sections.intro: Quick framing and check exposures.

items.label: Snap single frames
items.text: with chosen exposure, gain, and binning, with optional save.

items.label: Continuous stream mode
items.text: for live framing.

items.label: Plate solve from preview
items.text: solve the current frame and sync or center.

items.label: Full image tools
items.text: stretch controls, statistics, star annotations, and crosshair/grid/pixel readout (shared with the Studio viewer).

sections.title: AUTORUN
sections.intro: A straightforward sequence runner against the current target.

items.label: Frame list editor
items.text: rows of exposure x count per filter, gain, and binning.

items.label: Polaris Shutter
items.text: start and stop control with live progress.

items.label: End-of-session actions
items.text: warm the camera and cooler off, park or go-home, send the focuser to zero, and optional host shutdown.

items.label: Flat Wizard sub-tab
items.text: automated flat-field acquisition with binary-search exposure per filter, a trained-exposure cache, and per-rig defaults.

sections.title: PLAN
sections.intro: ASIAIR-style whole-night planning: queue several targets, each with its own frame list, run in order with automatic slew and plate-solve-center.

items.label: Multiple targets per plan
items.text: added from catalog search, manual RA/DEC, the current mount position, or framed visually in the Sky map.

items.label: Per-target frame lists
items.text: and a first-light delay.

items.label: Scheduling
items.text: start now or at a clock time; end when all frames are done, at astronomical dawn, or at a set time.

items.label: Plan-level automation
items.text: auto guiding, auto cooling (with target temp), per-target or initial auto-focus, and auto meridian flip with exposed flip tuning (minutes-after, recenter, autofocus-on-flip).

items.label: End actions
items.text: warm and cooler-off, park or go-home, focuser-to-zero, and a confirm-gated host shutdown.

items.label: Elevation chart
items.text: of each target across the night for sanity-checking the order.

items.label: Global plan library
items.text: saved plans live in a global library, runnable with any active rig, and can be exported and imported as JSON to share between hosts.

sections.title: LIVE
sections.intro: Real-time electronically-assisted-astronomy stacking that builds an image as frames arrive.

items.label: Continuous integration
items.text: with live alignment (star matching) and a growing preview.

items.label: Per-frame pre-processing
items.text: optional calibration (auto-matched master dark/flat/bias) and GraXpert background extraction applied before each frame is added, running wherever the stack runs: in the browser via WebAssembly and WebGPU, or server-side through the GraXpert CLI or the RK3588 NPU.

items.label: OSC color stacking
items.text: automatic for one-shot-color cameras.

items.label: Auto re-focus and re-center triggers
items.text: kick off an auto-focus or a re-center when HFR drifts or the target wanders.

items.label: Save the current stack
items.text: to FITS at any time, into a dedicated stacked folder.

items.label: Client-side compute offload
items.text: on a slow server (Pi 2/3) the stacking math can run in your browser via WebAssembly instead of the host.

items.label: Server-side capture loop
items.text: an optional, experimental mode that runs the capture loop on the server, so the stack keeps building even if the browser disconnects.

items.label: Reference-frame suggestions
items.text: to improve alignment quality.

sections.title: VIDEO
sections.intro: High-frame-rate capture and stacking for planets, the Moon, and the Sun.

items.label: SER capture
items.text: high-fps video recording (tested to about 100 fps) with ROI subframing.

items.label: Frame-quality analysis
items.text: Laplacian-variance scoring to rank frames.

items.label: Lucky-imaging stacker
items.text: keep the best N% of frames and stack them.

items.label: Slew preview inset
items.text: a small live view while you center the planet.

sections.title: ADV
sections.intro: A full NINA-style, tree-based sequencer for complex automated nights.

items.label: Tree of containers, instructions, conditions, and triggers
items.text: with drag-and-drop editing.

items.label: Instruction library
items.text: camera (cool/warm/expose), mount (slew/park/find home), focuser, filter wheel, guider (start/stop/dither), flow control (wait-until-time), and more.

items.label: Loop conditions and event triggers
items.text: meridian flip, auto-focus on temperature, HFR, or time, and other operational triggers.

items.label: JSON serialization
items.text: save, load, and share sequence documents.

sections.title: STUDIO
sections.intro: Browse, calibrate, and integrate your captured frames on the host.

items.label: Frame browser and library
items.text: scan and organize captured frames.

items.label: Master generation
items.text: build master darks, flats, and bias frames.

items.label: Calibration
items.text: apply masters to light frames.

items.label: Batch stacking
items.text: register and integrate a set of lights into a master, with progress reporting.

items.label: Channel combine
items.text: merge per-filter masters into one RGB image, with RGB compose (no luminance needed), LRGB (Lab or ratio combine when you have a luminance master), and PixelMath for narrowband palettes (HOO, SHO).

items.label: Color calibration
items.text: Siril-style and plate-solve-driven: background neutralization (zero-config), manual (background patch and white-reference patch), and PCC, Photometric Color Calibration against the bundled APASS DR10 star catalog for science-grade color.

items.label: Quick processing
items.text: debayer, background extraction, noise reduction, and sharpening passes.

items.label: Star colour repair
items.text: fix the one-sided colour fringe (a blue or magenta cast with a dark notch) that some one-shot-colour cameras leave on bright stars, using sub-pixel channel alignment and radial colour and luminance symmetry repair. Neighbour-aware for crowded fields, with a before/after montage of the brightest stars.

items.label: Crop tool
items.text: with a drag picker.

sections.title: EDITOR
sections.intro: A Lightroom-style finishing editor for your master image.

items.label: Slider-based adjustments
items.text: grouped into Light, Color, Effects, and Detail, with an auto-tune button for a sensible starting point.

items.label: Non-destructive
items.text: edits are stored in a sidecar .edit.json next to the source file; the original is never overwritten.

items.label: AI section
items.text: run GraXpert BGE, Denoise, and Deconvolution from inside the editor with a before/after slider.

items.label: Star removal
items.text: split a master into starless and stars-only images with an in-browser AI model (nox or starrem2k13, both MIT, or the opt-in StarNet++), launched from the FILES toolbar. Optional halo reduction cleans the rings and halos around bright stars. Writes _starless and _stars FITS and opens a before/after comparator.

items.label: Image Blend
items.text: recombine two same-size images with an independent blackpoint/midtones/highlights stretch per layer, a blend mode (Screen, Add, or Lighten), and opacity. The PixInsight ImageBlend-style finish for putting stretched stars back onto a separately-stretched nebula, with a live preview and full-resolution 16-bit _blend FITS output.

items.label: Export
items.text: to JPEG, PNG, or TIFF with quality and resize options.

items.label: Auto-stretch
items.text: ported from GraXpert (15% background, 3-sigma) as the default display stretch.

sections.title: AI inference
sections.intro: GraXpert's AI models run on whatever hardware is fastest, with no per-frame cloud calls.

items.label: Models
items.text: Background Extraction (BGE), Denoise (v2 and v3), and Deconvolution (stars and objects).

items.label: Star-removal models
items.text: nox and starrem2k13 (both MIT, bundled) plus the opt-in StarNet++ (NonCommercial). All are FP16-quantized so they run in the browser on phones and tablets via WebGPU, or on WASM.

items.label: On-device model downloader
items.text: pull ready-made .onnx models onto the device from the bundled SourceForge catalogue or your own bucket, with SHA-256 verification and no Docker or Python on the host (Settings, AI inference, Download models).

items.label: In-browser inference
items.text: onnxruntime-web uses the client device's GPU (WebGPU) or WASM SIMD; the server just hosts the .onnx files.

items.label: Server-side CLI fallback
items.text: GraXpert on the host, when you prefer the host to do it.

items.label: NPU acceleration
items.text: on Rockchip RK3588 boards (RKNPU2, e.g. the Orange Pi 5 Pro) and Qualcomm Hexagon boards (QAIRT, e.g. the Radxa Dragon Q6A), the background-extraction and denoise models run on the NPU about 5x faster than the CPU, freeing cores for live stacking. Automatic, with a CPU fallback.

items.label: Pick your accelerator
items.text: choose Auto, NPU, GPU, or CPU for the GraXpert AI ops. On boards with more than one accelerator, a Vulkan GPU lane (via ncnn) runs alongside the NPU.

items.label: OpenCL GPU backend
items.text: image math can offload to the SBC GPU where available.

items.label: RGB FITS support
items.text: throughout the AI pipelines.

sections.title: FILES
sections.intro: Server-side file browser.

items.label: Browse, download, and manage
items.text: captured frames and outputs on the host.

items.label: Upload images
items.text: into Studio or Editor as an entry point for processing.

sections.title: SETTINGS
sections.intro: Global configuration, host management, and connectivity.

items.label: Profiles and location
items.text: observer location (with a first-run setup modal), units, and app-wide preferences.

items.label: Appearance
items.text: theme and font picker.

items.label: Network mode (Hotspot and Station)
items.text: ASIAIR-style WiFi panel. The Pi ships as a hotspot on first boot so you can reach it without a monitor; flip it onto your home WiFi with a 30-second try-and-revert safety net.

items.label: Remote access (Relay)
items.text: TLS-tunneled access to your rig from outside the LAN, with optional DuckDNS and Let's Encrypt.

items.label: HTTPS setup
items.text: one-click self-signed certificate (port 5001) so client devices get WebGPU and multi-thread WASM for in-browser AI.

items.label: Authentication
items.text: login and first-run wizard protecting the UI and API.

items.label: Remote terminal
items.text: embedded SSH terminal (xterm.js) to manage a headless host from the browser, with a one-click launcher for the native raspi-config or armbian-config tool.

items.label: Clock sync
items.text: push the browser's UTC to a Pi without an RTC.

items.label: Equipment simulator
items.text: built-in fake telescope, camera, focuser, and filter wheel that renders real stars at the simulated position, so plate solve, auto-focus, and live stacking all work without hardware.

items.label: Benchmark
items.text: synthetic workloads to compare hardware (CPU, GPU, and a GraXpert denoise pass on the board's NPU) with a saved results history.

items.label: Software self-update
items.text: on Pi/SBC .deb installs, a status-bar badge appears when a newer GitHub release exists; one click downloads the matching .deb, installs it, and reloads on the new version. No password needed, authorized via a scoped PolicyKit rule.

items.label: Version rollback
items.text: Settings, Power, Roll back version reinstalls any recent release over the running one (downgrade included), online or offline through the relay; handy if an update misbehaves.

sections.title: HELP
sections.intro: In-app guidance.

items.label: Step-by-step tutorials
items.text: capture-to-export, first-night checklist, and specific workflows (LRGB mono, planetary, PCC).

items.label: Troubleshooting accordion
items.text: and links to the full user guide.

items.label: Report a problem
items.text: opens a pre-filled GitHub issue or discussion with client and server diagnostics attached.

sections.title: Always-on UI
sections.intro: Features present across every panel.

items.label: Top status bar
items.text: connection badges (INDI, Alpaca, PHD2), camera temperature, live-stack frame count, client-device battery, clock, guider dither/settle state, a global sequence-abort button, the update badge, and the debug-log badge.

items.label: Activity and transfer chips
items.text: live network throughput, in-flight uploads and downloads, image-frame and exposure progress.

items.label: Debug log
items.text: every server log, HTTP request, toast, and browser exception collected in one panel, filterable and exportable as JSONL for bug reports.

items.label: Multi-instance tabs
items.text: manage several Polaris hosts from one browser.

items.label: Dismissable health chips
items.text: for example Raspberry Pi undervoltage warnings.

items.label: One-command .deb install
items.text: for Debian and Ubuntu on arm64 SBCs (Raspberry Pi, Orange Pi, Radxa) and on x86-64 PCs; the package handles every dependency, the systemd unit, indi-web, and user setup.

items.label: Windows and Linux
items.text: hosts both supported.

items.label: Docker image and compose
items.text: for containerized deployment.

items.label: Plate-solving
items.text: via ASTAP and other solver backends.

items.label: Plugin system
items.text: for extending the app.
